answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making admission a slow, collateralized graft into a living garden of established identities. A newcomer posts a time-locked ivory bond that only matures after peers attest a streak of original work; until then the applicant sits on an island of limited privileges, unable to multiply votes or harvest settlement. Forging many such bonds would lock capital in parallel with no early payout, so flooding the network becomes self-punishing rather than profitable.
